en.title: Change Digits One at a Time to Match an Array
en.description:
Corresponding integers in the two arrays have the same number of digits. Each operation increases or decreases one decimal digit of some integer in arr1 by 1, without going outside 0..9, without carrying, and without moving digits. Find the minimum number of operations to make it identical to arr2. This is the operation explained digit by digit in the source's first example.

The standard input/output format was compiled by this site; added numeric bounds and the encoding for no-solution cases are explicitly marked and do not claim to be the source's original constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n, the second line contains arr1, and the third line contains arr2. 1≤n≤100000, 1≤element≤10^9, the two arrays have the same length, and each pair of corresponding integers has the same number of decimal digits.
en.explanation: The examples give 10, 17 and 8 respectively. In the second example, the original output 16 and the explanation's 15 are both incorrect: 7+4+0+6=17.
hints: For each number, add up the absolute differences between the corresponding digit characters position by position.
